findings.claim: The rewritten recovery-label clause attributes the label's landing site to the drill-down path, which never sets it — `pending_recovery` is assigned in family 2 only — and cites a case that contains no `observe` as the exemplar of "the `extract` the drill-down was asked for".
findings.evidence: specs/001-browser-contract.md:130-135: "Both skip PAST an observe and land on the next attempt of any other kind, which is usually the extract the drill-down was asked for ... and recovery-replan-postcondition is the shape where it is the ONLY step the new plan has". src/browser/agent.py:833 is the only assignment of pending_recovery, and it is inside family 2's act->replan branch; the drill-down branch (agent.py:743-791) sets only the pending note. evals/adversarial/recovery-replan-postcondition.json has stub plans [click(bad postcondition), extract] then [extract] — no observe, no drill-down, so nothing 'skips past' anything there; the label lands directly on the family-2 replan's first step. ADR-019 section 2 carries the same conflation.
findings.repro: grep -n 'pending_recovery' src/browser/agent.py -> 682, 694, 697, 833; only 833 assigns "recovery", and it is unreachable from the drill-down branch. Compare with specs/001-browser-contract.md:130-135.
findings.acceptance: The clause separates the two statements: the label defers past an observe and lands on the next non-observe attempt (which in recovery-replan-postcondition is a bare extract with no drill-down involved, and in recovery-label-lands-on-the-extract is the extract the drill-down's replan returned while a family-2 recovery is in flight).
